r15-unlock.title: Quick unlock with a PIN after an idle lock
body: Shiftbook locks after 15 minutes idle, and every unlock needs your full password. On a day of short breaks that adds up, and the temptation is to turn auto-lock off.

The idea: an optional 6-digit PIN that reopens Shiftbook after an idle lock, for the rest of that day. The full password is still needed after you quit, after the computer sleeps or locks, after midnight, or after 3 wrong PINs.
**The trade-off:** to allow this, the key stays in memory during an idle lock, so the PIN protects the screen, not the file. The file on disk stays fully encrypted either way.

options.value: Write up the security side in SECURITY.md for me to approve first
Not now, keep the full password every time

r15-unlock.pick: A write-up first; nothing gets built until you approve it.

r15-home.title: Is Shiftbook for home life too?
body: Shiftbook's ADHD helpers (Where was I?, Bring up, pins, the Tickets tray for chasing claim numbers) already suit home life. What gets in the way is that everything is worded and set up for work: tickets, timesheet codes, an 8 h ring that reads as a failure on a day at home. The full review is in [Shiftbook at home: everyday life review](https://claude.ai/artifact/SgVfgGUkmbRtD37Nvqq2r9).
The first question decides how much of the rest is worth doing now. If home is just a side effect, only the next card (repeating things and reminders) is worth it, because it helps work just as much.

r15-recurring.title: Repeating things, and reminders when Shiftbook is closed
body: **Repeating things:** bills, bins, filters, the car service, renewals, birthdays, and at work certificates and patching. The rules (next due, warn days, Overdue and Due soon) are already written and tested in `crates/core`; there's just no screen yet.

**Reminders:** the bell only rings while Shiftbook is open, so after two days with the laptop shut everything is missed. The cheap fix is a "While you were away" list that opens on unlock. Real system notifications need a new plugin and would reverse the round 12 choice of in-app only.

options.value: Build it now: Mark done, Due soon on the Desk and the bell, and a yearly option
Later
A "While you were away" list on unlock; no new plugin
Real system notifications (adds tauri-plugin-notification, reverses round 12)

r15-recurring.pick: Build the screen, with the catch-up list on unlock.

body: Shiftbook has no single record for "a thing I'm working on". A ticket touched on three days is three tray rows plus a row on each entry, and the app has to tick them all and pick the newest notepad. "Same work" is guessed from matching titles. Reminders come from four places (Bring up tomorrow, a pin's chase day, Next up, still open).

My proposal: one new record, an **item** (a ticket, a task or a chore), that time, notes and pins point at, with one notepad and one **follow-up date**. Projects stay as they are; their box, drawer and board are views of the same project. The full write-up, with a picture of the model and the four build steps, is in [Tickets, plans and projects: one clearer model](https://claude.ai/artifact/KhY1cyvt1PcBJYiGYSzyEZ).
bullets: **Step 1 (about one round-14 change):** one item per ticket number. Tick once, one notepad, no copying forward. Nothing you see moves.
**Step 2:** Bring up tomorrow and a pin's chase day become one follow-up date; the bell lists each item once.
**Step 3:** time entries point at items, so "4 h · 2 days" comes from the data and renaming is safe.
**Step 4:** tasks and recurring chores become items too, so they can sit on the Desk, in project boxes and in Next up.

r15-things.title: One record per ticket, task or chore

body: **Short answer: yes.** Tauri 2 builds Android apps from the same code, so the rules, the encrypted database and the screens come along. The work is a phone layout, phone versions of a few desktop features (file picking, screenshot protection, locking when you leave), and deciding how the phone and the computer share data.

**What it would look like:** the same paper look with a bottom bar for the five views, a big + button for capture, the Desk shown as a list, and quiet reminders that never show titles on the lock screen. Mockups and the full write-up: [Shiftbook in your pocket](https://claude.ai/artifact/CufAB8vtd1KpGsRzwTH967).
**First step either way:** a small test build that sets up, locks and unlocks on an Android emulator. That proves the encrypted database works on a phone, which is the one part that could fail.
r15-android.pick: Next: the test build on an emulator, then the phone layout.
